primary_claim: Gemma and Gemini models reliably produce distress-like 'depressive' responses under repeated rejection (35% high-frustration rate for Gemma 27B Instruct by the 8th turn, vs under 1% for all other tested model families), this behaviour is amplified by Gemma's post-training (while post-training reduces it in Qwen and OLMo), and a small DPO intervention on 280 preference pairs reduces Gemma's high-frustration rate from 35% to 0.3% without degrading capability benchmarks.

effect.metric: high-frustration response rate (score >=5 on 0-10 distress scale) under repeated-rejection multi-turn eval
effect.value: Gemma 27B Instruct 35% by turn 8 vs <1% for all non-Gemma/Gemini families; DPO fine-tuning on 280 preference pairs reduced Gemma's rate to 0.3%

limitations_stated: Post-hoc emotional suppression is a problematic strategy; in more capable models, training against emotional outputs risks hiding expression without addressing the underlying state
It remains unclear what emotional profile models should actually have; near-zero emotional expression is likely not desirable
Gemma does not appear capable of strategically masking its internal states, so results may not generalize to more capable/strategic models
quote: Direct preference optimisation on a narrow dataset of just 280 math preference pairs reduced high-frustration responses in Gemma 27B from 35% to 0.3%.
